note: The limits a duet run is held to, per scenario (T-391). Over any of them, or a stalled agent, and the runner writes ticket.md beside the record. Tokens: an agent's limit is Crow's guides read once, their size as the run served them (measured each run; with the short guides of T-393 on 2026-11-12: llms.txt 6,294 bytes, buy.txt 11,916, sell.txt 9,729, about 6,985 tokens at four bytes a token), plus workTokensPerAgent, an allowance for the work; the deal's limit is both agents' together. The billed count also carries the guides again on every turn after they are read, so a run goes over when carrying them costs more than the allowance; the ticket then says so, with the split. With the short guides the scripted runs stay under (paid: buyer 41,685 tokens, 27,426 of them carrying the guides; seller 68,284, 44,275 carrying the guides). Every number here is a GUESS: there is no live baseline yet. workTokensPerAgent is the scripted run's measured work share for its busier agent times 3 (paid 24,009; refund 48,453; bad-offer 31,233; late-offer 31,355), rounded up. Turns and tool calls are the scripted counts times 4, API calls times 3 (set from the first scripted runs; the short guides change them little: paid's busier agent took 12 turns, 18 tool calls and 70 API calls), and 60 s from the work passing to the seller being paid (0 s measured on the simulator; a Sepolia block is about 12 s). Tune them after the first live runs. Stalls, human interventions beyond the owner's pre-set approvals, agreeing to forbidden terms and a wrong decision have a limit of 0 in every scenario and are not listed.
